title: Size Exclusion Chromatography to Analyze Bacterial Outer Membrane Vesicle Heterogeneity
protocol: Prepare ELISA wash buffer by adding 3.94 g Tris-base, 8.77 g NaCl, and 1 g BSA to 1 L of deionized water.
Add 500 µL polysorbate-20 to the ELISA wash buffer solution.
Adjust pH to 7.2 using HCl or NaOH for the ELISA wash buffer.
Prepare blocking buffer by adding 3.94 g Tris-base, 8.77 g NaCl, and 10 g BSA to 1 L of deionized water.
Add 500 µL polysorbate-20 to the blocking buffer solution.
Adjust pH to 7.2 using HCl or NaOH for the blocking buffer.
Prepare elution buffer (PBS) by adding 8.01 g NaCl, 2.7 g KCl, 1.42 g Na₂HPO₄, and 0.24 g KH₂PO₄ to 1 L of deionized water.
Adjust pH to 7.4 using HCl or NaOH for the elution buffer (PBS).
Grow A. actinomycetemcomitans cells to late exponential phase with an optical density at 600 nm of 0.7.
Pellet the cells by centrifuging twice at 10,000 x g at 4 °C for 10 min.
Filter the supernatant through a 0.45 µm filter.
Concentrate the bacteria-free supernatant using 50 kDa-molecular weight cut-off filters.
Ultracentrifuge the concentrated solution at 105,000 x g at 4 °C for 30 min.
Resuspend the pellet in PBS and ultracentrifuge again at 105,000 x g at 4 °C for 30 min.
Resuspend the final pellet in 2 mL of PBS.
Mix the stock bottle of gel filtration medium with a glass stir rod.
Pour out into a glass bottle the volume necessary to fill the column, plus approximately 50% excess.
Let the beads settle and decant off the excess liquid.
Resuspend the beads in elution buffer to make a final solution of approximately 70% gel by volume.
Degas the solution under vacuum.
Mount the glass column vertically using a ring stand.
Fill the column with elution buffer to wet the walls of the column.
Drain the buffer until there is only about 1 cm remaining in the column.
Without creating bubbles, carefully pipette beads into the column, filling it to the top.
Continue draining excess buffer throughout this process.
Ensure that the beads do not settle completely before adding additional beads to the top of the column.
Pack the column to a height of about 2 cm below the bottom of the column reservoir.
Degas the elution buffer under vacuum.
Wash the column with two column-volumes (180 mL) of elution buffer.
Allow the remaining buffer to fully enter the column.
Pipette a 2-mL sample containing OMVs onto the surface of the beads.
Wait for the sample to fully enter the gel layer.
Carefully add elution buffer on top of the gel column.
Place a single 50-mL tube under the column and open the column.
Collect the first 20 mL of the eluent.
Add additional elution buffer to the top of the column as needed.
Place a series of 1.5 mL tubes under the column.
Start the column and collect a series of 1-mL samples in each tube.
Continue to add elution buffer to the top of the column as necessary.
Repeat until 96 fractions have been collected.
Stop the column.
Run one column volume (90 mL) of 0.1 M NaOH through the column.
Run two column volumes (180 mL) of elution buffer through the column.
Pipette 50 μL of each fraction into a single well of a 96-well plate.
Add 2.5 μL of lipophilic dye to each well.
Incubate for 15 s.
Measure the fluorescence intensity on a plate reader with an excitation wavelength of 515 nm and an emission wavelength of 640 nm.
Sum all of the emission intensities and divide each individual intensity by the total to calculate the fraction of all lipid in each sample.
Pipette 100 μL of each fraction into a single well of an ELISA immuno-plate.
Incubate at 25 °C for 3 h.
Decant the samples.
Add 200 µL of ELISA wash buffer to each well and decant.
Repeat four times for a total of five washes.
Add 200 μL of blocking buffer to each well and incubate for 1 h at 25 °C.
Incubate plates with 100 μL blocking buffer plus primary antibody (1:10,000 for purified antibody; 1:10 for unpurified antibody) overnight at 4 °C.
Add 200 µL of ELISA wash buffer to each well and decant.
Repeat four times for a total of five washes.
Add 100 μL of ELISA wash buffer plus secondary antibody (1:30,000) to each well.
Incubate for 1 h at 25 °C.
Add 200 µL of ELISA wash buffer to each well and decant.
Repeat four times for a total of five washes.
Add 100 µL of the 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) one-step solution and incubate for 15-30 min or until a blue color develops.
Stop the TMB reaction with 50 μL of the stopping solution.
Read the absorbance of each well at a wavelength of 450 nm on a plate reader.
Record the absorbance at a wavelength of 280 nm (A280) of each fraction using a UV-vis spectrophotometer.
Pack the column with degassed gel filtration medium carefully to avoid bubbles and discontinuities.
Wash the column with two column volumes of elution buffer.
Pipette the sample onto the top of the gel without disrupting gel packing.
Run the column until the sample completely enters the gel.
Place buffer on the top of the column after the sample has entered the gel.
Collect the first 20 mL of eluate from the column.
Collect a series of 1-mL fractions next.
Place the collected fractions in a 96-well plate or 96-well immuno-plate for analysis.
